summary: Specifies the Quote of the Day service, which sends a short message without regard to the input. It is an Internet Standard for hosts that choose to implement it.

plainLanguage.summary: The Quote of the Day service sends a short message without considering what the client sends. It can reply over a TCP connection or send one quote back in a UDP datagram.

questions: what is the quote of the day protocol
how does qotd work over tcp
how long should a qotd message be
subtitle: Defines a simple TCP or UDP service that replies with a short quote.

tldr.problem: A simple response service can help people debug and measure network connections.
tldr.mechanism: A server on port 17 sends a short message over TCP and closes the connection, or returns a quote in response to each UDP datagram.
tldr.outcome: The quote has no required syntax; the RFC recommends ASCII printing characters and fewer than 512 characters.

today: RFC 865 is listed as an Internet Standard in the unit metadata. The metadata lists no RFC that updates or obsoletes it.

sections.title: A Short-Message Service
sections.content: The Quote of the Day service sends a short message without regard to the input. The RFC describes it as a useful debugging and measurement tool for hosts that choose to implement it.
sections.plainLanguage: The service returns a short message even though it does not use the request's contents. It can help check a network connection.

sections.title: TCP and UDP Replies
sections.content:
For TCP, the server listens on TCP port 17. After a connection opens, it sends a short message, ignores any received data, and closes the connection after the quote.

For UDP, the server listens on UDP port 17. When a datagram arrives, the server replies with a datagram containing a quote and ignores the received data.
sections.plainLanguage: With TCP, the server sends a quote and closes the connection. With UDP, each incoming datagram receives one datagram containing a quote.

sections.title: Quote Content
sections.content: The RFC defines no specific quote syntax. It recommends ASCII printing characters, space, carriage return, and line feed. A quote can occupy one line or several, but it should be less than 512 characters.
sections.plainLanguage: The message can be any short quote rather than a fixed format. The RFC recommends readable characters and keeping it under 512 characters.
